By Malay Mail First Published: Wednesday, 18 Nov 2026 3:37 PM MYT × Subscribe to Newsletter
 Subscribe KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh both registered firm objections to granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon for house arrest during the Sept 18 Pardons Board meeting, according to purported minutes of the confidential session leaked online.
 Excerpts of the document surfaced on the social media page of a former DAP lawmaker detailing high-level deliberations over the controversial royal clemency order.
 The authenticity of the uploaded papers has not been independently verified by Malay Mail.
 According to the leaked transcript, the attorney-general maintained his consistent stance that Najib should remain incarcerated in prison until 2028. Dusuki reportedly argued that house arrest is wholly absent from statutory legislation and remains “foreign” to the Malaysian legal system, citing a judicial precedent set by High Court Judge Alice Loke.
 He cautioned that sanctioning home detention would trigger severe domestic and international repercussions, particularly harming political stability, the national economy, foreign investment, and Malaysia’s international standing, firmly insisting that Najib “should continue serving his sentence”.
 The minister in the Prime Minister’s Department overseeing Federal Territories, an executive portfolio held by Yeoh, endorsed the attorney-general’s dissenting position, reaffirming her prior opposition to the pardon.
 Although the minutes do not explicitly identify Yeoh by name, the record notes that after the board examined the draft terms of the home detention arrangement, both she and the attorney-general declined to provide feedback “given that they disagree with the conditional pardon”.
 Despite their pushback, the minutes indicate that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, who chairs the Federal Territories Pardons Board under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, was “inclined” to grant the conditional pardon, permitting Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest upon settling an RM50 million fine.
 The document also details a procedural dispute over who should formally sign the release instrument. Pointing to counterfeit pardon orders circulating on social media and citing Section 14 of the Representation of Powers Act 1956, the minister suggested delegating the signature to an alternative official, such as the Cabinet secretary, given the acute political sensitivities involved.
 While the AG requested time to evaluate the statutory provision, an officer on special duties to the King argued that it was inappropriate for the Chief Secretary to the Government to execute the document as he did not attend the meeting, with the monarch affirming that the civil service head is not a board member.
 Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain cautioned that appointing an alternate signatory would provoke wider controversy by creating the impression that the minister had boycotted the proceedings. The King subsequently ruled that Yeoh must sign the order as the minister responsible for Federal Territories administration.
 The leak arrives amid an escalating push within government for official disclosure. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail informed Parliament on Nov 12 that he would propose declassifying the minutes to the Cabinet, while Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil confirmed that ministers have sought formal legal counsel from the attorney-general.
 Najib was transferred to his private residence earlier this month to begin serving his house arrest, which runs until August 2028.
